beats.narration_text: Dumela. This is Liam, in for Bear, with a short film for INFO seventy-three seventy-five, Branding and AI. Engineers tend to ask how to build it better. Now that building is cheap, the question is what else you have to show.

at building?

beats.motion_claim: The writer types the build-only question and corrects it: be seen for what you build.

qc.sparse_reason: Hesitant-writer bookend: the correction is the motion.

beats.narration_text: Three terms. A costly signal: something that's hard to fake cheaply, so it tells people apart. Brand: the choices that decide whether the right stranger can find your work and see it's for them. And ship: put it in front of real users, at a public link.

terms.meaning: hard to fake cheaply, so it tells people apart
choices that let the right stranger find your work
real users, at a public link

qc.sparse_reason: TERMS card: three prerequisites, one line each.

beats.narration_text: A creative engineer is an engineer who noticed the costly signals shifted, and invested accordingly. The work comes down to four verbs. Ideate. Build. Brand. Ship.

shot.motion_claim: Four kraft slabs land one by one as each verb is spoken, labelled Ideate, Build, Brand, Ship; a small box lands on the first.

beats.narration_text: Ideate is the hardest move, and the one AI can't do for you yet. Hand the tools a specification and they'll build it. They can't tell you whether it's worth building. That takes talking to real people, and finding a real gap.

beats.narration_text: The mistake I see most: pick a technology you want to learn, build a project around it, then try to glue a user need on afterward. You get a competent thing nobody wanted. It shows Build. It doesn't show Ideate.

beats.narration_text: Build is the verb AI cheapened. Real production systems still need deep technical judgment. But a repo on GitHub no longer sets you apart. Build is necessary. It isn't sufficient.

beats.narration_text: Brand is where engineers push back hardest. So think of an API with no documentation. It computes. It returns the right values. But the developer who needs it can't tell what it's for, so it's useless. Documentation isn't decoration. It's what connects the API to the people who need it. Brand is documentation for your career.

shot.visual_intent: A dark API block on the right; a cable from a second block on the left reaches toward it and stops short; a white doc page attaches to the API, the cable connects, and lights come on ('API', 'docs').

beats.narration_text: In practice, Brand is a handful of choices: who it's for, how it's positioned, the voice, the look. Together they decide whether a stranger who needs your work can find it, and see it's for them. Your work can't speak for itself if the person it's for never finds it.

beats.motion_claim: A stranger types what they need; three results drop in; only the one that says who it's for gets picked.
beats.why_card: Search IS the idea (a stranger finding your work); results arriving IS the claim; a drawing can't show search better.

beats.narration_text: Ship means a public link, people who found it, and feedback from real use. Not a commit. Not a class demo. Shipping teaches you the most, because every guess you made gets tested the moment real users touch it.

shot.visual_intent: The box rides out through an open gate ('public'); three curved feedback lines draw back from the right with dots travelling along them; the box's tape turns on ('feedback').
shot.motion_claim: The box rides out through an open gate ('public'); three curved feedback lines draw back from the right with dots travelling along them; the box's tape turns on ('feedback').

beats.narration_text: So score yourself honestly on each verb, one to five, where five means public evidence a stranger could see. For Ideate, that's user research. For Build, a deployed project. For Brand, a clear audience. For Ship, real users.
beats.motion_claim: A lens steps down the rubric verb by verb as each is spoken.
beats.why_card: The rubric IS a table; the lens stepping row by row IS scoring yourself verb by verb.

beats.narration_text: It works at company scale too. Anthropic was founded in 2021 by former OpenAI researchers, and put a published safety method, Constitutional AI, at its front door. OpenAI does similar technical work, but leads with capability, and a mission of AGI that benefits all of humanity. Similar tech. Two brands. Two audiences.
beats.motion_claim: Two tabs: Anthropic's panel, then the pill slides and OpenAI's panel replaces it.
beats.why_card: The idea IS compare A then B; the tab switch IS the comparison. Rows are verified wording only.

beats.narration_text: And it works for one person. A clear audience, a clear position, and the work to prove it decide who can find you, want you, and hire you. Not a company. A career.

shot.visual_intent: The four slabs again, Build ghosted; the box hops across all four and gets the terracotta tape on Ship ('a career').
